requirement_results.command: PostgresC3Service is a real isinstance match for every sealed C3 Protocol: GovernedCommitPort, CanonicalReadPort, RevisionPort, RecoveryPort, OutboxRelayPort
a real commit persists state, revision and a matching unacknowledged outbox envelope atomically against real PostgreSQL
a repeated commit with the identical idempotency key and command content returns the byte-identical receipt marked replayed=True, without advancing the revision again
reusing an idempotency key with different command content is rejected with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT
a commit whose expected_revision does not match the real current revision is rejected with REVISION_CONFLICT
two distinct commands racing the same aggregate/expected_revision on real PostgreSQL connections: exactly one succeeds, the other receives a real REVISION_CONFLICT

a real subprocess crash mid-commit (os._exit after the aggregate upsert, before the commit/idempotency/outbox rows) leaves zero visible state and an empty outbox, then a fresh commit of the identical command succeeds normally

a real simulated corruption fixture (the outbox row for a real commit deleted directly against the database) is repaired by reconcile(), re-deriving the missing row from the commit row's own denormalized fields
a real committed outbox envelope is claimed and then acknowledged, after which it no longer appears in a fresh claim
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: The state-merge semantics (a shallow dict overlay of canonical_delta onto the current state) are deliberately minimal, matching 'the smallest contract-compliant implementation'; no domain-specific deep-merge or field-level conflict rule is implied or required by the sealed ports.

_crash_after on PostgresC3Adapter.commit_transaction (re-exported via PostgresC3Service.commit) is a keyword-only, underscore-prefixed test-only fault-injection hook, mirroring spikes.c3_atomicity.oracle's already-accepted crash_stage pattern; it is never exercised through the sealed GovernedCommitPort Protocol, which declares only commit(self, command).

reconcile()'s repair path is defense-in-depth: under normal operation the single-transaction design makes a partial c3_commit row (missing its idempotency or outbox row) structurally impossible, since a crash mid-transaction rolls everything back. This task proves recovery from both real failure classes: a genuine process crash (transactional rollback, zero partial state) and a genuine simulated corruption after the fact (a derived row deleted, then repaired).

This slice implements the full C3 canonical-commit surface (all 5 sealed ports) rather than a narrower subset; OutboxRelayPort's claim/acknowledge are included since they are needed to prove the outbox half of atomicity end-to-end, not left as a separate future task.

A genuine architectural fitness violation (AFF-002/AFF-006: a direct PostgreSQL client import outside an adapters/ subtree) was found and fixed before this evidence was sealed -- see the commands log above -- establishing the first ocor-runtime/src/ocor_runtime/**/adapters/ precedent this delivery has needed.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test begins from service.reset() (a real TRUNCATE against the live schema) so a fresh run from a clean or partially-populated database converges to the same state -- verified directly by 4 consecutive full test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them, including the real process-crash and real simulated-corruption drills, both of which are themselves rollback/recovery proofs by construction.
